21. HIRSUTISM IN YOUNG WOMEN:

•presence of Coarse hairs
•5 - 15%
•Can be Idiopathic - no underlying endocrine disorder

Pathophysiology:

•total hair follicles 50million
•scalp = 100,000 - 150,000
•few follicles form after birth
•decline after 40 years

Types of hairs:

•lanugo: Fetus - Shed in 4months after birth
•Villus: <2cm, longer than lanugo - all over the body - non pigmented
•terminal: coarse - scalp, eyebrow, eyelashes Axilla, Pubic areas.

Phases of Hair Growth:

•Anagen: active. growing phase - determine length of hairs.
•Catagen: involuting, stop growing.
•Telogen: Resting - hairs shedding.

Independent of androgens:

•eyebrow, eyelashes occipital region, lateral side of skull.

Low levels of androgens:

•public hairs and axillary hairs

Need high levels of androgens:

•Chest, Back, Lower abdomen, Face, Upper thigh.

CAUSES OF HIRSUTISM:

1.PCOS:

70-80% Cause of Hirsutism

•insulin Resistance -> insulin levels increase androgen levels by Theca cells -> SHBG
•30 - 75% women with PCOS are OBESE.

2.Acanthosis Nigerican:

3% of women with androgen excess

•severe insulin Resistance.
•can present with virilization.
•difficult to treat.

3.Androgen Secreting tumors:

•rare - 1/300-1/1000 women with Hirsutism have Androgen secreting tumors.
•suspect if:

1. Rapid onset of symptoms.

2. virilization.

3. cushingoid features.

Diagnosis on clinical presentation:

⇨suppression or / stimulation Tests are misleading.
⇨>50% Adrenal Tumor with hyperandrogenism is malignant.

4.CAH non classic:

1.5 - 2.5% of hyperandrogenic women.

5.Drugs:

•Androgenic effects - danazol, Anabolic steroids.
•Non-Androgenic effects
- Phenytoin, minoxidil, diazoxide.
-Streptomycin, psoralen, penicillamine.
-High dose steroids.

6.Idiopathic:

•all other causes ruled out.
•No hormonal abnormalities, normal periods, ovaries, and no evidence of Tumors.

Evaluation:

HISTORY

EXAMINATION

  • →drugs
  • →wt. changes
  • →change in facial contour.
  • →Family history like premature male balding
  • →DM
  • →extent type & pattern of hairs
  • →virilization signs
  • →thyroid enlargement signs
  • →galactorrhea
  • →Abdominopelvic masses
  • →obesity
  • →Cushingoid features
  • →Systemic illness

 

 

 

Diagnosis:

→Subjective assessment by Ferriman Galway Score:
-0 – 4 on each area (0 no of hair, 4 Extensive hair)
-Total 9 areas

1: Upper lips 2: Chin 3: Chest 4: abdomen 5: lower Abd & pubic area 6: upper back

7: thighs 8: Forearms 9: Lower back

-score >6 => significant
→Severity of Hirsutism:
-Score 8-15 Mild

without other features like Menstrual problem treat cosmetically.

-Score >15 Mod – Severe
-investigate the cause
-Free Testosterone >1.5-2ng/dl => Neoplasm.
-17α Hydroxyprogesterone in

(1). All Non classic CAH

(2). PCOS but <200mg/l

-pelvic USG - PCOD, Neoplasm.
-DHEA sulphate - adrenal Source.

 

Management:

→Reassurance.
→wt loss & life style.
-5-10% wt loss => 4-5% improvement in Hirsutism. within 6months
-1st line in Obese PCOS @ least for 6months.

→Cosmetic Methods:
1.Waxing: Discouraged - risk of folliculitis
2.Bleaching: useful
3.Plucking: Discouraged
4.Shaving: Blunt hairs
5.Depilatory creams: useful, chronic use, skin irritation.

→Physical Methods:
1.Electrolysis:
•destruction of individual hair follicle via electrode.
•Expensive
•18months to 4yrs r required to treat
•painful
•practical for limited areas of skin
•cause burns, Depigmentation, skin scarring.
2.laser Photo thermolysis or selective Photo thermolysis:
•Appropriate for light skinned women. As they require lower Radiation pulses. Dark women => laser with cooling devices.

•Covers wider area.
•Less painful.
•Reduces hair density permanently by 30% after 3-4 sessions.
•In PCOS density of hirsutism by laser.

 

Hormonal Therapies:

•Conversion of Terminal hairs to villus hairs.
•Long t/m - requiring 9-12months

 

→COCP:
•Don't reverse Hirsutism, need for shaving by 50% & inhibit Progression.
•SHBG + inhibits LH hormone & Testosterone.
•Drosperinone containing pills (Yasmin) more effective
• risk of Endometrial Hyperplasia.
•Cycle regularity

 

→Cyproterone acetate CA:
•Decrease LH => decrease Testosterone & Androstenedione
•Act as an androgen Antagonist Peripherally.
•Lower Ferriman Score by 15 – 40% within 6months,

Max effect 6 – 12months.

•Diane 35 (EE 35mg, 2mg CA)
-S/E: wt gain, Depression, fatigue, sexual dysfunction
-Altered LFT’s (do LFT’s before CA), VTE more than 2nd generation COCP.
•Androcur high dose CA 50mg.
•Given in women who r resistant to low dose CA along with EE for short term use.

 

→Spironolactone:
•Aldosterone Antagonist + mild Diuretics

Androgen inhibitor + structurally similar to progesterone.

•1/20th efficiency for dihydrotestosterone receptor binding so high doses r required.
•100mg/ day is superior to low dose CA 12.5mg/day & Finasteride 5mg/day for up to 12months.
→Finasteride: inhibitor of 5alpha reductase.
•Used for t/m of BPH.
•Similar efficiency as CA but few S/E.
•Feminization of female fetus
→Flutamide: Non-steroidal anti androgens, Block androgen receptors & at high doses inhibit production of androgens.
•Used in t/m of CA prostate.
•S/E: Greenish tinge to urine, Dry scalp and skin, abnormal LFT's (LFT's should be checked before t/m).
•250 - 500mg/day

 

→Insulin Sensitizers:
•Improve hirsutism in PCOS
•Effective in both Obese and lean women

 

→Cell cycle Inhibitors:
•Eflornithine inhibits ornithine decarboxylase in skin.
•Topical use twice/day.
•Rapidly absorbed (within 5min).
•Reduce hair growth by 60%.
•Stop if no benefit after 4months.

S/E: acne, photosensitivity.

→GnRH-A loss of BMD 2-8% over 6months
